text.text_excerpt: This is where we spent most of our bar time last trip. It wasn't even close to where we were staying either, ha. We went there to primarily do our laundry and then started going even when we didn't have any. A few pool tables and dogs are allowed. Panhandler alert, I just tell them even kookier stories, tho, hehe. Don't forget the mandatory burger, mm yummy stuff.

The first time I visited Igor's was in the late 1990s. The drinks were great & the burgers were huge. Also, leave it to New Orleans to cater to the individual who prioritizes having drinks & bar food over doing laundry. Great hole in the wall. I found myself back at Igor's recently & the place is EXACTLY as I remembered it...down to the red lighting. A lot of post-Katrina New Orleans feels decidedly different to me, but not this hang. For that, I am grateful. The Cheese Burger is still affordable, huge, & delicious (the Cheese Fries rock, too). I didn't get a drink this time, but I didn't hear any of the other patrons complaining. Service was great & the ambience was relaxed & inviting. I...

Igor's was only a short 5 min or less walk from my Airbnb on St Charles ave & was sparsely populated from about 8:30pm-midnight on a Sunday. It was my last night in town & my friends & I settled here after dinner to hang & chill with some drinks & music since bourbon beat us down the night before. Bloody Mary's here are way more SPICY than others we had in town but they are cheap. As are many of the other drinks. Bartender was a one woman machine & very personable. She was cooking up burgers, dancing, & pouring drinks throughout the evening. After a few ginger & Jamison's I probably spent $20 on music via the digital jukebox. All in all it's a divey place you can burn a few hours listenin...
